intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, when crowds are thinner and the light is magical. Hire a local tuk-tuk driver based near Siem Reap's Old Market area to navigate the vast complex efficiently. Given a late Day 1 arrival, begin this experience on Day 2 morning after a short rest. Stay near Pub Street or the Old Market to minimize travel time to the temples.

experiences.name: Bayon Temple & Angkor Thom Exploration
experiences.description: Discover the enigmatic stone faces of Bayon and the ancient walled city of Angkor Thom on your second temple day. This is best done in the late afternoon to avoid midday heat and tour bus crowds. Staying in the Old Market district of Siem Reap puts you within 15–20 minutes of the site, making afternoon visits practical even after a late arrival the previous evening.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Royal Palace & Silver Pagoda
experiences.description: Visit the stunning Royal Palace and the Silver Pagoda, home to a floor of 5,000 silver tiles and a life-size gold Buddha. Located in the heart of Phnom Penh near the riverside, this experience is ideal for the mid-morning hours. Book accommodation in the Riverside or BKK1 district to walk or take a short ride to the palace, maximizing your time especially if arriving by domestic flight from Siem Reap midday.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Sanloem Beach Day
experiences.description: Take a ferry from Sihanoukville to the pristine Saracen Bay on Koh Rong Sanloem for crystal-clear waters and white sand beaches. This island escape is a perfect contrast to the historical sites. Ferries depart mid-morning, so staying near the Sihanoukville ferry pier the night before ensures you catch the earliest boat and maximize beach time. Budget includes round-trip ferry and a light beachside lunch.

experiences.name: Khmer Cooking Class in Siem Reap
experiences.description: Join a hands-on Khmer cooking class in central Siem Reap, learning to prepare traditional dishes like fish amok and green mango salad. Classes typically include a guided market visit to Psar Chaa (Old Market) before cooking, making it a rich cultural and culinary experience. Scheduling this on Day 2 afternoon or Day 3 morning is ideal since it is walkable from Old Market area hotels, perfectly suiting a traveller who arrived late on Day 1.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Siem Reap Boutique Stay. Once settled, take a leisurely walk along Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chas) area to get oriented. Browse local stalls, pick up a SIM card, and exchange currency at a local money changer for the best rates.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the vibrant Night Market on Sivatha Boulevard. Enjoy the atmosphere, browse handmade crafts and souvenirs, and soak in your first Cambodian evening. Head to bed early to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) from a street stall near the Old Market for around $1–2.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khmer Kitchen Restaurant near Pub Street — a beloved budget-friendly spot serving authentic Khmer dishes like amok and lok lak for $3–5 per dish.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange USD at local money changers near Old Market for better rates than the airport. Cambodia widely accepts USD. Buy a local SIM (Smart or Metfone) for around $2–3 with data.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn and head to Angkor Wat for sunrise — one of the most iconic experiences in Southeast Asia. Arrive by 5:15 AM to secure a good spot by the reflecting pool. Explore the outer galleries and bas-reliefs as the sun rises over the temple towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Angkor Thom complex, including the Bayon Temple with its famous 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon, Phimeanakas, and the Terrace of the Elephants. Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the day (around $15–18) to navigate the large complex efficiently.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Angkor National Museum (entry ~$12) for cultural context on what you saw today, or skip to save money and watch a free Apsara dance performance preview near Pub Street.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks or grab a baguette (French colonial influence) and coffee from a street vendor near the temple entrance for under $2.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the local food stalls just outside the Angkor complex near the South Gate — rice with grilled chicken or pork for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Try Cuisine Wat Damnak's more affordable sister street stalls, or dine at Psar Leu Market food court for authentic local food at $2–4 per plate.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass for $62 — far better value than single-day ($37) if you plan to visit multiple days. Wear light, breathable clothing and bring sunscreen and a hat. November weather is dry and pleasant (~25–30°C).

day_by_day.morning: Use your Angkor Pass to explore the outer temples: Ta Prohm (the 'Tomb Raider' temple with trees growing through ruins), Banteay Kdei, and the peaceful Sras Srang reservoir. Ta Prohm is best visited early before tour groups arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Preah Khan temple, a sprawling jungle monastery with atmospheric corridors and carved doorways. Then head to Neak Pean, a unique island temple set in a large baray (reservoir).
day_by_day.evening: Back in Siem Reap, visit the Artisans Angkor workshop (free entry) near the Old Market to watch craftspeople carve stone, weave silk, and lacquer wood — a fascinating cultural experience supporting local artisans.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a Khmer breakfast of bai sach chrouk (pork and rice) from a local market stall for $1.50.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from the market — fruit, bread, and snacks — to eat among the temple ruins.
meals.dinner: Try Sugar Palm Restaurant on Taphul Road for traditional Khmer cuisine; budget around $5–8 for a satisfying meal.

day_by_day.notes: Bring at least 1.5 liters of water per person. Modest dress (covered shoulders and knees) is required at all temples. Renting a bicycle ($2–3/day) is a fun and cheap way to reach some closer temples.

day_by_day.morning: Use your final day on the Angkor Pass to visit Banteay Srei, a 10th-century temple renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings — considered the jewel of Khmer art. Located about 25 km from Siem Reap, hire a tuk-tuk or join a shared tour ($5–8).
day_by_day.afternoon: On the way back, stop at the Landmine Museum (entry $5) — a sobering and important cultural experience run by a former child soldier, documenting Cambodia's tragic history with landmines and ongoing demining efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Cambodian Cultural Village (entry ~$10) near the airport road for a condensed overview of Cambodia's diverse ethnic groups, traditional architecture, and folk performances — great for history and culture lovers.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your guesthouse if breakfast is included, or try a local bakery for a coffee and pastry for $1–2.
meals.lunch: Stop at a local restaurant in Banteay Srei village for a simple rice dish with vegetables or fish for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Head to the Siem Reap Night Food Market near the river for a variety of Khmer street food — grilled meats, spring rolls, and fresh fruit shakes for $3–5 total.

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is a longer trip — start early. The Landmine Museum is deeply educational and highly recommended for history-minded travelers. Donations beyond the entry fee are welcome.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Floating Villages of Tonle Sap Lake — take a shared boat tour to Kampong Phluk (dry season access, ~$15–20 including transport and boat). Walk through the stilted wooden village and learn about life on Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and explore the local Psar Leu Market (Central Market) — a working local market away from tourist areas. Bargain for fresh produce, spices, local snacks, and cheap clothing. Great for cultural immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost traditional Apsara dance performance. Several restaurants like Smile of Angkor offer dinner shows (~$12–15 with dinner), or check for free community performances at local temples.

meals.breakfast: Grab a Khmer-style breakfast of num banh chok (rice noodles with green fish curry) from a market stall for $1.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local restaurant near Psar Leu Market — fish amok or stir-fried vegetables with rice for $2–3.
meals.dinner: If attending a dinner show, it covers dinner. Otherwise, enjoy grilled corn and skewers from riverside street vendors for $2–4.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tonle Sap boat tour through your guesthouse or a local agency the night before. Avoid overpriced tourist boat operators near the lake — negotiate or book in advance. The lake is at its fullest and most impressive October–January.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early morning bus from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approximately 6 hours, ~$6–8 with Giant Ibis or Mekong Express — reliable budget-friendly operators). Depart by 7:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh around 1:00–2:00 PM. Check in to a budget guesthouse in the BKK1 or Riverside area ($8–15/night). Head to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda complex (entry $10) — a stunning example of Khmer royal architecture with gilded spires and sacred Buddha statues.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sisowath Quay (Riverside Promenade) as the sun sets over the Mekong and Tonle Sap rivers. Browse street food stalls, watch locals exercise and socialize, and enjoy the lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure or grab food at the Siem Reap bus station — rice porridge or a sandwich for $1–2.
meals.lunch: Eat on the bus or stop at a roadside restaurant during the journey for a simple rice dish for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Dine at Friends Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) on 13th Street — a non-profit training restaurant with excellent Cambodian tapas at $4–7 per dish, supporting street youth.

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets at least one day in advance through your guesthouse or online. Giant Ibis is slightly pricier but the most reliable. Store valuables safely during the bus journey. Phnom Penh guesthouses fill up — book ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison, entry $8) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge prison camp. A deeply moving and essential historical experience to understand Cambodia's tragic 20th-century history. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk (~$10–12 round trip) to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial (~17 km from city center, entry $6 including audio guide). The audio guide is excellent and deeply informative. Pay respects at the memorial stupa.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and decompress with a walk through the Russian Market (Psar Toul Tom Poung) — a great place for cheap souvenirs, local textiles, street food, and people-watching. Prices are better here than tourist markets.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a French-influenced Cambodian breakfast of baguette with pâté and iced coffee at a riverside café for $2–3.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local eatery near Tuol Sleng for a simple rice and curry dish for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Try Romdeng Restaurant on Street 174 — another non-profit restaurant serving traditional Cambodian cuisine including exotic dishes like tarantula, for $5–8 per dish.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Killing Fields visits are emotionally heavy — take your time and be respectful. Photography rules are posted throughout. Consider hiring a local guide at Tuol Sleng for deeper context ($5–10). These sites are essential for understanding modern Cambodian history.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the National Museum of Cambodia (entry $10) near the Royal Palace — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture, including pre-Angkorian bronzes and sandstone carvings. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Sihanoukville by bus (~4.5–5 hours, $8–10 with Mekong Express or Capitol Tours). Depart around noon, arriving by late afternoon. Sihanoukville is Cambodia's main beach hub.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a budget guesthouse or beach bungalow on Otres Beach ($10–20/night — quieter and more relaxed than the main town). Take a sunset walk along the beach and enjoy the sea breeze.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your Phnom Penh guesthouse or a nearby café — fruit, eggs, and coffee for $2–3.
meals.lunch: Grab food at the bus station or eat on the road at a rest stop for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Enjoy fresh grilled seafood at a beachside restaurant on Otres Beach — grilled fish, prawns, and rice for $5–8.

day_by_day.notes: Sihanoukville's main Victory Beach area has changed significantly due to development — Otres Beach (Otres 1 and 2) remains the most peaceful and budget-friendly option. Alternatively, consider taking a ferry to Koh Rong Samloem island for a more pristine beach experience ($15–20 ferry).

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning relaxing on Otres Beach — swim, sunbathe, read, or rent a kayak ($5–8/hour) to explore the coastline. November is part of the dry season, so expect calm, clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a snorkeling trip or island-hopping boat tour to nearby islands (Koh Ta Kiev or Koh Russei) — organized day tours cost $15–25 per person including snorkeling equipment and lunch. The coral reefs and crystal-clear water are stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Otres Beach for a bonfire beach barbecue if available, or enjoy a quiet dinner at one of the laid-back beachside bars. Watch the stars — light pollution is minimal on Otres Beach.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a tropical fruit platter and smoothie at a beachside café for $2–3.
meals.lunch: Lunch is typically included on island-hopping tours — fresh BBQ seafood on the beach.
meals.dinner: Dine at Holy Crab or a local seafood shack on Otres Beach — whole grilled crab or lobster for $8–12 (a splurge worth it for a beach day).

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect coral ecosystems. Bring cash as ATMs near Otres Beach are limited. Negotiate boat tour prices with multiple operators before booking. November is excellent for beach weather in Sihanoukville.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final relaxed morning on Otres Beach — swim, pick up last-minute souvenirs from beach vendors, or rent a bicycle ($2–3/day) to explore the surrounding area and local fishing villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to Phnom Penh by bus (depart by 12:00–1:00 PM, ~5 hours, $8–10) for any onward international flights, or extend your beach stay if your departure allows. Use the journey to review photos and journal memories.
day_by_day.evening: If spending a final night in Phnom Penh, revisit the Riverside for a farewell dinner. Browse last-minute souvenirs at the Night Market near the riverside. Reflect on 10 incredible days in Cambodia.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a full Western or Khmer breakfast at your guesthouse or a beachside café — eggs, toast, fresh juice for $3–4.
meals.lunch: Eat at a roadside stop during the bus journey for $2–3, or pack snacks from the market.
meals.dinner: Final dinner at a riverside restaurant in Phnom Penh — try fish curry or a Khmer BBQ platter for $5–8 as a farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 10 days: Accommodation $80–150, Transport $50–70, Food $80–120, Entry fees $60–80, Activities $40–60 — Total approximately $310–480 USD for a comfortable budget trip. Keep $20–30 emergency cash. Cambodia is a safe, welcoming destination — enjoy every moment!

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Siem Reap Boutique Stay and check in.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll through the Pub Street area and the Old French Quarter to get oriented. Visit the Psar Chaa (Old Market) to browse local crafts, spices, and souvenirs. A gentle introduction to Siem Reap's atmosphere without overexerting after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Pub Street and Alley West for the lively night scene. Enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance at a nearby cultural venue such as Koulen Restaurant or Smile of Angkor for an immersive first evening.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light meal at a café near the hotel after check-in — try Khmer Kitchen Restaurant for affordable local dishes like fish amok and lok lak.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak or Haven Restaurant — mid-range Khmer cuisine with excellent ambiance; budget around $10–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Exchange currency at the airport or a local money changer near Old Market. USD is widely accepted in Cambodia. Stay hydrated — November weather is generally pleasant with low humidity post-rainy season.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Angkor Wat (arrive by 5:30 AM for the iconic sunrise reflection over the moat). Explore the outer galleries, the bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central towers. Hire a licensed guide at the entrance for deeper historical context (~$20–25 for a half-day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom — the grand walled city. Visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Take a tuk-tuk between sites for convenience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap for a rest before heading out. Visit the Angkor Night Market for unique handicrafts, silk scarves, and handmade jewelry — great for souvenirs at reasonable prices.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel or grab a baguette and coffee from a street stall near Angkor Wat — French colonial influence makes baguettes a local staple.
meals.lunch: Lunch at one of the open-air restaurants near Angkor Thom's north gate — try a Khmer set meal with rice, soup, and stir-fry for $5–8.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant — upscale Khmer dining with traditional recipes; budget around $15–20 per person. Alternatively, Mahob Restaurant for authentic local flavors.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62) if you plan to visit the temples over multiple days — it offers the best value. Wear comfortable walking shoes, bring sunscreen, a hat, and a refillable water bottle. Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) to enter temple sanctuaries.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ta Prohm — the atmospheric jungle temple famously used in the Tomb Raider film, where massive tree roots engulf ancient stone walls. Then explore Banteay Kdei and the serene Srah Srang reservoir, perfect for quiet reflection and photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Banteay Srei, located about 25 km northeast of Siem Reap. This 10th-century temple is renowned for its extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings — considered the finest example of classical Khmer art. Hire a tuk-tuk for the round trip (~$15–20).
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop in Siem Reap to see local craftspeople creating silk, lacquerware, and stone carvings using traditional techniques. The shop is fair-trade and a great place to buy authentic souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Blue Pumpkin — a popular Siem Reap café known for fresh pastries, smoothies, and Western-Khmer fusion breakfasts.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a local market near Ta Prohm or a simple roadside stall — grilled corn, fresh fruit, and sticky rice are inexpensive and delicious.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Sugar Palm — a beloved mid-range restaurant specializing in traditional Khmer recipes passed down through generations; budget $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 3 uses the second day of your 3-day Angkor Pass. Start early (7:00 AM) to beat the crowds at Ta Prohm. Banteay Srei is smaller but incredibly detailed — allocate at least 1.5 hours there.

day_by_day.morning: Use the third day of the Angkor Pass to visit the remote Preah Khan temple — a sprawling monastic complex with long corridors and atmospheric moss-covered stonework. Then visit Neak Pean, an artificial island temple surrounded by a circular pool, and Ta Som with its iconic tree-covered eastern gateway.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Roluos Group — the oldest Khmer temples near Siem Reap (9th century), including Preah Ko, Bakong, and Lolei. These lesser-visited temples offer a quieter, more personal experience of Khmer history without the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Cambodian circus performance by Phare, the Cambodian Circus — a world-class social enterprise where young Cambodian artists perform acrobatics, theater, and music. Book tickets in advance (~$18–38 depending on seating).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel to prepare for a full temple day.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local family-run restaurant near the Roluos Group — simple Khmer dishes like bai sach chrouk (pork and rice) for $3–5.
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner at Vibe Café or Chanrey Tree Restaurant near Phare Circus — light Khmer tapas and cocktails in a relaxed setting.

day_by_day.notes: This completes your 3-day Angkor Pass. Roluos temples are about 13 km southeast of Siem Reap — factor in tuk-tuk travel time. Phare Circus is one of Cambodia's most highly recommended evening experiences and supports at-risk youth through arts education.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip on Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake. Visit a floating village (Kompong Phluk or Kampong Khleang) to see stilted wooden homes, floating schools, and local fishing communities. A guided tour costs $15–25 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Cambodian Cultural Village on the outskirts of Siem Reap — a living museum showcasing traditional Khmer architecture, ethnic minority villages, and cultural performances from across Cambodia's diverse regions.
day_by_day.evening: Travel day preparation: arrange a private car or bus transfer to Phnom Penh (approximately 6 hours by road or 45 minutes by domestic flight). If taking the evening bus (Giant Ibis or Mekong Express recommended — ~$12–15), depart around 7:00–8:00 PM and arrive late evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before checkout.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a floating restaurant on Tonlé Sap Lake — fresh grilled fish and river prawns with rice for $6–10.
meals.dinner: Early dinner at a Siem Reap restaurant before departure — try Kanell Restaurant for a final taste of Khmer cuisine in the city.

day_by_day.notes: Check out of the Siem Reap Boutique Stay today. Store luggage at the hotel if taking a late bus. The Giant Ibis bus is the most recommended mid-range option for the Siem Reap–Phnom Penh route — comfortable, reliable, and includes Wi-Fi. Book in advance online.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive in Phnom Penh (if traveling overnight by bus) and check into a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hotel near the riverside (BKK1 or Riverside District recommended — budget $30–60/night). After freshening up, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — a stunning complex of Khmer royal architecture with gilded spires, the Throne Hall, and the famous Silver Pagoda with its 5,000 silver floor tiles and life-sized gold Buddha.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia — the country's largest museum of cultural history, housing an extraordinary collection of Khmer sculptures, bronzes, ceramics, and ethnographic objects spanning from the pre-Angkorian period to the present. Then stroll along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant riverside scene. Walk along the promenade at sunset and visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — an Art Deco landmark from 1937 with a distinctive yellow dome, selling jewelry, clothing, and local goods.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast near the bus station or at the hotel — local rice porridge (borbor) with ginger and egg is a comforting morning option for $2–3.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Friends the Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) — a social enterprise training at-risk youth in hospitality; excellent Khmer tapas for $8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant — a mid-range social enterprise restaurant specializing in traditional Cambodian cuisine including exotic dishes like tarantula fritters if you're adventurous; $12–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Phnom Penh is Cambodia's capital and offers a rich blend of history, culture, and modernity. The Royal Palace may be partially closed during royal ceremonies — check the schedule in advance. The riverside area is safe and walkable in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21) — a former high school converted into a prison by the Khmer Rouge regime (1975–1979). This deeply moving and historically important site documents the atrocities of one of history's darkest chapters. Allow 2–3 hours and consider hiring an audio guide or survivor guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day trip to the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (The Killing Fields), located 15 km south of the city. This memorial site includes a Buddhist stupa containing thousands of skulls and bones, with an excellent audio guide narrating personal survivor stories. Return to the city by tuk-tuk.
day_by_day.evening: Decompress with a relaxing sunset cruise on the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers — many operators offer 1.5-hour cruises with drinks for $8–15. This provides a peaceful and reflective end to a heavy but important day.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a riverside café — egg baguettes and iced coffee are a popular Phnom Penh morning staple for $3–5.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Tuol Sleng — Café 360 or a nearby local eatery; keep it simple given the emotional weight of the morning.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Topaz Restaurant or Khéma Pasteur — French-Khmer fusion in a relaxed setting; a good way to wind down with quality food and wine; $15–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek are emotionally intense experiences — take your time, be respectful, and allow space to process. These sites are essential for understanding Cambodia's modern history and resilience. Dress conservatively and maintain a quiet, respectful demeanor throughout.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville by bus (Giant Ibis or Mekong Express — ~4 hours, $9–12) or by private taxi (~3 hours, $50–60 shared). Check into a mid-range beachfront guesthouse or boutique hotel on Otres Beach or Koh Rong area (~$30–55/night). Otres Beach is quieter and more scenic than the main Serendipity Beach area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on Otres Beach — a long, relatively uncrowded stretch of white sand with calm turquoise waters. Rent a sun lounger ($2–3) and enjoy the peaceful coastal atmosphere. Take a swim in the warm Gulf of Thailand waters.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Otres Village area — a laid-back strip of beach bars, seafood restaurants, and bungalows. Watch the sunset over the Gulf of Thailand and enjoy the relaxed beach town vibe.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the bus or grab a quick bite before departure in Phnom Penh.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside restaurant on Otres Beach upon arrival — fresh grilled seafood platter with rice and salad for $8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at one of the Otres Village beach restaurants — try Otres Nautilus or Samudera Seafood for fresh catch of the day; budget $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: November is an excellent time to visit Sihanoukville's coast — the rainy season has ended, seas are calm, and the weather is warm and sunny. Otres Beach is strongly recommended over Serendipity Beach, which has become more commercialized. Book accommodation in advance as Otres can fill up during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Koh Rong Samloem — one of Cambodia's most beautiful islands, just 45 minutes by speedboat from Sihanoukville ($25–35 round trip). Visit Saracen Bay or M'Pai Bay for pristine white sand beaches, crystal-clear water, and vibrant coral reefs. Snorkel among tropical fish and coral gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Koh Rong Samloem — hike across the island through jungle trails to reach quieter beaches on the other side. Alternatively, join a half-day snorkeling tour around the island's reef system ($15–20 including equipment).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sihanoukville by late afternoon speedboat. In the evening, visit the Serendipity Beach area for a lively sunset happy hour — many bars offer 2-for-1 cocktails during golden hour. Enjoy the contrast between the island's serenity and the coastal town's energy.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before catching the morning speedboat — toast, eggs, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch on Koh Rong Samloem at a beachside shack — fresh coconut, grilled fish, and fried rice for $6–10.
meals.dinner: Dinner back in Sihanoukville at Holy Cow Restaurant or a seafood BBQ stall on the beach — grilled prawns, squid, and fish with dipping sauces for $8–14.

day_by_day.notes: Book the speedboat to Koh Rong Samloem the evening before to secure your spot — Speed Ferry Cambodia is a reliable operator. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a dry bag for your belongings, and cash as ATMs are limited on the island. The bioluminescent plankton around Koh Rong Samloem is visible on dark nights — ask locals about night swimming spots.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Otres Beach — enjoy a leisurely sunrise walk along the shoreline. Take a last swim in the Gulf of Thailand and soak in the peaceful coastal atmosphere. Visit a local beach market for final souvenir shopping — handmade jewelry, sarongs, and local spices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, take the bus or taxi back to Phnom Penh International Airport (~4 hours) or Siem Reap (if flying domestically). Use travel time to reflect on the journey and organize photos and keepsakes. If time allows before departure, visit a final café for a traditional Cambodian iced coffee (kafe tuk doh ko) — a perfect farewell ritual.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cambodia. If your flight departs late evening, enjoy a final meal at the airport or a restaurant near Phnom Penh airport in the Toul Tom Poung (Russian Market) neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast at a beachside café — fresh tropical fruit platter, coconut pancakes, and iced coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the road or at a rest stop en route to the airport — packed snacks or a quick local meal.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the airport or a restaurant near your departure point — choose a Khmer dish you loved most during the trip as a final taste of Cambodia.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–3.5 hours travel time from Sihanoukville to Phnom Penh Airport plus 2 hours check-in time. Consider buying last-minute gifts at the airport — Cambodian silk, Kampot pepper, and Angkor Wat replicas are popular choices. Reflect on the incredible diversity of this 10-day journey: ancient temples, cultural depth, historical significance, and stunning beaches — Cambodia truly offers a balanced and unforgettable experience.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Siem Reap Boutique Stay with a welcome cold towel and refreshments in the vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in at Siem Reap Boutique Stay. After freshening up, take a leisurely private tuk-tuk tour through the charming streets of Siem Reap's Old French Quarter, exploring colonial architecture, local markets, and the Siem Reap River promenade. Visit the Angkor National Museum for an introductory immersion into Khmer history and the civilization behind Angkor Wat.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the vibrant Pub Street and Alley West area, then enjoy a welcome dinner at a top-tier Cambodian restaurant featuring refined Khmer cuisine with live traditional Apsara dance performance.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge)
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments and afternoon tea at the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak — one of Cambodia's finest restaurants offering a contemporary tasting menu of seasonal Khmer dishes with curated wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport pickup with hotel concierge in advance. Keep Day 1 light given travel fatigue. The Angkor National Museum closes at 18:00 so plan accordingly. Confirm Apsara dinner show reservation before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private guided tour to Angkor Wat to witness the legendary sunrise over the temple's iconic silhouette reflected in the lotus ponds. Arrive by 05:15 for the best vantage point. Explore the outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central sanctuary with your expert English-speaking guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom — the great walled city. Visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Enjoy a private picnic lunch arranged by the hotel in the shade of the ancient walls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a spa treatment at the in-house luxury spa — opt for a traditional Khmer herbal compress massage to ease temple-walking fatigue. Dinner at a refined rooftop restaurant overlooking the city.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light breakfast box prepared by the hotel (croissants, fruit, coffee, juice) enjoyed at Angkor Wat
meals.lunch: Private gourmet picnic lunch with cold-pressed juices, fresh spring rolls, and Cambodian sandwiches arranged by the hotel concierge
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant — upscale Cambodian fine dining with signature dishes like amok, lok lak, and grilled river fish with a curated cocktail menu

day_by_day.notes: Angkor Pass (3-day or 7-day) must be purchased the evening before at the official ticket office — hotel concierge can assist. Wear light breathable clothing and carry sunscreen and insect repellent. Bring a hat for afternoon exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to Ta Prohm — the atmospheric jungle temple famously featured in Tomb Raider — where ancient fig and silk-cotton trees dramatically intertwine with stone ruins. Follow with a visit to Preah Khan, a sprawling temple-monastery with long columned corridors and intricate carvings, often less crowded than the main circuit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the remote and exquisite Banteay Srei temple, known as the 'Citadel of Women,' featuring the finest pink sandstone carvings in all of Angkor. En route, stop at a local artisan village to observe traditional silk weaving and wood carving craftsmanship. Visit the Landmine Museum to learn about Cambodia's modern history.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cocktail experience at a rooftop bar with panoramic views of Siem Reap. Followed by dinner at a boutique restaurant specializing in French-Khmer fusion cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the hotel — fresh tropical fruits, eggs benedict, Cambodian rice porridge (bobor), freshly brewed Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a curated local restaurant near Banteay Srei — try fresh Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) and grilled meats in an open-air garden setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Malraux — a refined French-Cambodian bistro in a beautifully restored colonial villa with an extensive wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is approximately 25 km from Siem Reap — arrange a comfortable private air-conditioned vehicle for this excursion. The Landmine Museum is a sobering but important cultural stop; photography is respectful and encouraged in designated areas.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat excursion on the Tonlé Sap Lake — one of Southeast Asia's most important freshwater ecosystems and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Visit the floating villages of Kampong Phluk, where stilted wooden houses rise dramatically above the water. Observe the daily lives of local fishing communities and explore flooded mangrove forests by small wooden canoe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and boutique — a social enterprise training underprivileged Cambodians in traditional Khmer arts including lacquerware, stone carving, and silk painting. Browse and purchase authentic handcrafted souvenirs. Spend the remainder of the afternoon at leisure or enjoy a private yoga session arranged by the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private Apsara dance performance arranged at a heritage venue, followed by a multi-course royal Khmer banquet dinner inspired by ancient palace cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh smoothie bowls, Cambodian banana pancakes, eggs to order, and premium Cambodian single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on the boat during the Tonlé Sap excursion — grilled fish, river prawns, and seasonal vegetables prepared by a local cook
meals.dinner: Royal Khmer banquet dinner at Shinta Mani or a comparable heritage venue — featuring amok trey, samlor korko, and steamed sticky rice with mango for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Water levels on Tonlé Sap in November are typically receding post-monsoon — the floating villages are fully accessible and scenery is lush. Wear shoes that can get wet for the canoe portion. Artisans Angkor purchases directly support local artisan families.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided exploration of the lesser-visited outer Angkor temples: Beng Mealea — a spectacular jungle-engulfed temple 68 km east of Siem Reap that remains largely unrestored, giving a true sense of archaeological discovery. Explore its collapsed galleries, hidden chambers, and moss-covered towers with your expert guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Koh Ker — a remote 10th-century capital featuring a dramatic seven-tiered sandstone pyramid (Prasat Thom) rising above the jungle canopy. This UNESCO-listed site is one of Cambodia's most impressive yet least-visited archaeological complexes. Private vehicle required for this full excursion.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap by early evening. Relaxing evening at the hotel — enjoy cocktails at the hotel bar and a lighter, casual dinner at a trendy gastropub or wine bar in the Old Market area.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — continental selection with fresh tropical fruits, pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch prepared by the hotel, enjoyed in the shade near Beng Mealea or Koh Ker — artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, tropical fruit, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Dinner at Embassy Restaurant & Lounge — a stylish Siem Reap hotspot with creative cocktails, sharing plates, and a sophisticated atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Beng Mealea and Koh Ker together make for a long day trip (approx. 2–3 hours driving each way combined). Start early by 07:00. Hire a comfortable private SUV. Both sites require sturdy walking shoes as terrain is uneven. Bring extra water and sun protection.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap by private vehicle or domestic flight to Sihanoukville (or Koh Rong Samloem island) — Cambodia's premier beach destination. If flying, the journey takes approximately 1 hour; by road, approximately 6 hours via National Road 4. Check into a luxury beachfront resort on Koh Rong Samloem or at a high-end Ream Bay resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the beach resort and spend the afternoon unwinding on pristine white sand beaches. Enjoy a private snorkeling session in the crystal-clear waters of the Gulf of Thailand, exploring vibrant coral reefs and tropical marine life with a certified guide.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the beach terrace. Enjoy a romantic open-air beachfront dinner under the stars with fresh-caught seafood grilled to perfection.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Siem Reap before departure — full spread of Cambodian and Western options
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort upon arrival — fresh tropical fruit platters, grilled fish tacos, and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: Beachfront dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — whole grilled lobster, tiger prawns, fresh crab, and Cambodian-spiced fish with imported wines

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flights in advance if opting for air travel (Siem Reap to Sihanoukville). For Koh Rong Samloem, a speedboat transfer from Sihanoukville port is required (approx. 45 minutes). Recommended luxury resorts: Song Saa Private Island or Koh Rong Samloem's Saracen Bay Resort. November weather is generally dry and sunny on the coast.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided kayaking and island-hopping excursion around Koh Rong Samloem and neighboring uninhabited islands. Explore hidden lagoons, mangrove channels, and secluded white sand coves accessible only by water. Snorkel at a pristine coral reef with a marine biologist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a luxurious beach spa experience — choose from a traditional Cambodian massage, a coconut body scrub, or a couples' treatment in an overwater or beachside pavilion. Spend the remainder of the afternoon at leisure on the beach with a good book and chilled beverages.
day_by_day.evening: Unique bioluminescent plankton night swimming experience (seasonal, typically strong Nov–Jan) — wade into the warm sea after dark and watch the water glow electric blue around your movements. Return for a late dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — açaí bowls, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, tropical juices, and barista coffee served on the beachfront terrace
meals.lunch: Casual beachside lunch at a resort cabana — fish and chips, fresh ceviche, mango salad, and cold-pressed tropical juices
meals.dinner: Intimate candlelit dinner on a private section of the beach arranged by the resort — chef's tasting menu featuring local seafood with sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Bioluminescent plankton viewing is best on darker nights away from artificial light — request the resort to arrange this experience. Kayaking excursion should be booked through the resort's activity desk the evening before. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only to protect the coral ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure on the beach — optional stand-up paddleboarding, sunrise yoga on the sand, or a peaceful meditation session arranged by the resort wellness team. Explore the island's jungle interior on a short guided nature walk to observe tropical birds, butterflies, and native flora.
day_by_day.afternoon: Speedboat transfer back to Sihanoukville, then private vehicle transfer to Kampot — a charming riverside colonial town approximately 1.5 hours east. Check into a boutique luxury riverside retreat. Explore Kampot's beautifully preserved French colonial architecture and laid-back riverside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise along the Kampot River on a private wooden boat, sipping locally produced Cambodian wine or craft cocktails as the sun dips behind the Elephant Mountains. Dinner at a riverside fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast on Koh Rong Samloem — fresh tropical fruits, eggs to order, Cambodian rice porridge, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch in Sihanoukville or en route to Kampot — fresh seafood at a quality beachside restaurant
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rikitikitavi or Baraka — Kampot's finest riverside dining establishments offering creative international and Cambodian cuisine with premium wine lists

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is famous for its world-renowned Kampot pepper — one of the world's finest. Look for opportunities to visit a pepper plantation. The riverside town has a relaxed, bohemian atmosphere that contrasts beautifully with the busier coastal areas. Book the riverside boutique hotel well in advance — options include The Columns or Mekong Retreat.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to a Kampot pepper plantation — learn about the cultivation, harvesting, and grading of Cambodia's celebrated pepper from the farmers themselves. Participate in a pepper-tasting session and purchase premium peppercorns to take home. Follow with a visit to the Phnom Chhngok Cave Temple — a sacred limestone cave housing a 7th-century brick sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Kep — a sleepy seaside town 25 km from Kampot, once the playground of Cambodian royalty and French colonial elites. Visit the famous Kep Crab Market and explore the ruins of abandoned royal villas reclaimed by jungle. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon at Kep Beach or the tranquil Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) by short boat transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot for a final evening. Enjoy a private cooking class with a local Cambodian chef, learning to prepare authentic Khmer dishes using freshly sourced ingredients including Kampot pepper. Dine on what you've prepared.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Kampot — fresh fruit, baguettes with local honey and jam (French colonial influence), eggs, and strong Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Iconic fresh crab lunch at Kep's famous crab market shacks — steamed crab with Kampot green pepper sauce, a bucket-list Cambodian culinary experience
meals.dinner: Private Khmer cooking class dinner — dishes prepared include fish amok in coconut, beef lok lak, green mango salad, and banana blossom curry, paired with local Cambodian craft beer or wine

day_by_day.notes: The crab market at Kep is a must-do culinary experience — arrive by 12:00 for the freshest selection. Rabbit Island boat trips are short (15 min) and inexpensive. The cooking class should be pre-booked through the hotel concierge. Kampot pepper plantation visits are best in the morning when it's cooler.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cambodia — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Take a peaceful sunrise walk along the Kampot River promenade or enjoy a final spa treatment. Visit the Kampot Traditional Music School (if open) to hear performances of traditional Khmer instruments and support local cultural preservation efforts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private vehicle transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport (approximately 2.5–3 hours from Kampot) or back to Siem Reap if departing from there. En route, stop at a roadside stall to pick up last-minute Kampot pepper, palm sugar, and local handicrafts as premium souvenirs. Airport farewell with VIP lounge access if available.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cambodia — carry with you the memories of ancient temples, pristine beaches, vibrant river towns, and the warmth of Khmer culture and hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final hotel breakfast — full spread with fresh tropical juices, pastries, eggs, Cambodian coffee, and seasonal fruits
meals.lunch: Lunch en route to the airport — stop at a quality restaurant in Phnom Penh or a roadside gem serving authentic Cambodian cuisine
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours for the Kampot to Phnom Penh airport transfer to account for traffic. If departing from Siem Reap, a domestic flight from Phnom Penh is needed — book in advance. Consider purchasing Kampot pepper, silk scarves, Artisans Angkor pieces, and locally produced Cambodian rum or wine as premium gifts. Ensure all Angkor temple passes and receipts are kept as souvenirs.
